title: Finite-stage pro-etale internal Hom preserves the finite-Tor constructible category without separatedness
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $q=p^a$ and $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0=\mathbf F_q$. Let $\ell\ne p$ be a prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and let $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], without a separatedness assumption. On the small pro-etale site $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with constant coefficient ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ be the full subcategory of the derived category of $A_T$-module sheaves consisting of complexes with bounded constructible cohomology [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]: for each such complex $K$ there are integers $u\leq v$ such that $K\otimes_A^L F$ has zero cohomology outside $[u,v]$ for every $A_T$-module sheaf $F$ placed in degree zero.

For every $K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, the ambient derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$.

source.place: General etale finite-Tor preservation assertion, transferred to the pro-etale site by thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible in the same directory; the extracted domain argument is step 1 of the returned lem-trf-exceptional-internal-hom-exchange split. No site-perfect or separatedness hypothesis is used.

proof.text:
Write $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for site comparison. Since $\ell
e p$, its image in $k$ is a unit, whose image in every structure ring of $T$ remains a unit; hence $\ell$ is invertible on $T$. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii), choose $K',L'\in D^b_c(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and isomorphisms $
u_T^*K'\cong K$, $
u_T^*L'\cong L$. Choose Tor intervals $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ for $K,L$. Clause (ii) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] applied separately to these two isomorphisms gives the same intervals for $K',L'$ on the etale site. Its hypotheses hold: both representatives are bounded, hence bounded below, and the pro-etale objects are bounded constructible of the stipulated Tor amplitudes. Thus $K',L'\in D^b_{ctf}(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$; no site-perfectness is assumed.

source.place: Clause (ii), together with lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude(ii) in sk-cor-pe-finite-tor-comparison; etale-origin and Tor-reflection reduction

proof.text: Let $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the finite-type structure morphism. The spectrum of the field $k$ has one point, so every open cover has a member covering that point and is reduced to a finite cover. Apply [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] to $a_T$ with this quasi-compact target, obtaining $m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ bounding all fibre dimensions. The unique fibre is $T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k\cong T$: projection has inverse $(\operatorname{id}_T,a_T)$. Consequently $\dim T\leq m$. Empty $T$ is allowed by the cited statement; one may enlarge its bound to zero if needed.

source.place: Tag 0A3V, label lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension, applied to the structure morphism

proof.text:
Apply [thm-sf-hom-ctf] to $X=T$, $K=K'$ and $M=L'$ on the etale site. Its finite-field datum and coefficient ring are exactly the fixed $k$ and $A_{E,n}$. The scheme is finite type, the dimension bound is step 2, and step 1 gives bounded constructibility and the two Tor intervals. Its general clause, which has no separatedness or site-perfectness hypothesis, gives
$$
H'=R\mathcal Hom_A(K',L')\in D^b_{ctf}(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)
$$
with Tor amplitude in $I=[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$. We use this general clause, rather than the sharper clause for a site-perfect first variable.

source.place: General assertion and dimension-dependent interval; no use of the site-perfect sharper assertion

proof.text:
Apply [thm-sf-hom-comparison-constructible] with first argument $K'$ and second argument $L'$. Both lie on the etale site; its first argument is finite-Tor constructible by step 1 and its second is bounded constructible. No separatedness assumption occurs in its statement. It gives the canonical isomorphism
$$
\nu_T^*H'\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(\nu_T^*K',\nu_T^*L').
$$
Derived internal Hom is a functor contravariant in the first argument and covariant in the second [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Applying it to the two chosen isomorphisms from step 1 and their inverses identifies the right side with $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)$. Thus the target is isomorphic to $\nu_T^*H'$. This compares the ambient derived sheaf Hom objects and assumes no stalk formula for internal Hom.

source.place: Displayed internal-Hom comparison; transport through input isomorphisms by the derived-Hom bifunctor

proof.text: Apply clause (i) of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] to $H'$ and $I$. Its input is bounded constructible on the etale site and has that Tor interval by step 3; invertibility of $\ell$ was checked in step 1. It follows that $\nu_T^*H'$ is bounded constructible on the pro-etale site and has Tor amplitude in $I$. Step 4 supplies an isomorphism from this object to $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)$. Its cohomology maps identify all cohomology sheaves, preserving their finite bounds and constructibility. For every degree-zero pro-etale module sheaf $F$, tensoring this isomorphism with $F$ gives an isomorphism of the derived tensor products, whose cohomology consequently has the same vanishing outside $I$. This proves $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,L)\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$.

source.place: Clause (i), followed by invariance of cohomology and Tor-amplitude bounds under the specified isomorphism
